notes: MACRO, on the v2 plate kit. A print, what it means mechanically, and who
`who-it-hits` is the one repeat in the vertical formats: four or five
consequences told over TIME rather than as cards in one frame. Three
cards in a 9:16 column measure 33px type, under the readability floor.

A STATIC PLATE MAY HOLD. The ceiling was written when every plate in the kit boiled; 44 of the 140 are `playback: static` now, because a figure that moves is a figure being re-read. What keeps a data beat short is the ceiling itself, and it is set to what a seventy-second cut of ten beats actually gives each one.
NO ALTERNATE ORDER. `sign-off-first` put the closing card ahead of the hook,
and it could never have worked: the sign-off anchors nothing, so it took a
full even share of the opening (4.5-7 s) while the hook was spoken over it,
and the hook shot lost its anchor to the monotonic pass. The first second
is the ticker and the move. An order comes back when the narration says
where each beat starts, so a reordered cut still lands on its words.

alts.notes: The fifth treatment: the hook on a full field with the ticker at the foot, so the eye lands on the sentence before the chip. The same three slots. `hook-card-t4` is not here on purpose — it leads with the figure at 240pt, and the next beat is that figure.

What was expected over what came out, as two stacked panels. `body-1` is bound REQUIRED on purpose: the plate's caution is that without a real prior expectation it reads as a comparison against a number it invented, so the rotation only reaches for it when the script carries the consensus. The gap on the divider stays empty — it is a figure nobody wrote, and the pipeline does not compute one.

shots.notes: The statement itself, in the band drawn for it. NO `headline-stack` ALTERNATE HERE, unlike the SHORT: the stack needs a second headline, and a required bind is a field on the writer's form — which takes MACRO to thirteen, past the dozen at which a form is a document again and gets filled in like one.
How it actually works, in the card drawn for a term and its meaning.

One consequence per beat, full size. Three in a column measure 33px type, under the readability floor, so a chain at 9:16 has to be told over time. THREE, NOT FOUR. Every step of a sequence is a field on the writer's form, and a fourth consequence took the MACRO form to thirteen — past the dozen at which a form is a document again and gets filled in like one.

alts.notes: One consequence per beat as a term and its meaning. `$n-1` steps with the sequence exactly as the authored bind does.

THE OTHER WAY TO END. All three vertical formats closed on `structure/closing` every time, so every short in the channel signed off on the same drawing. The conclusion is a line worth pulling out by definition, and `quote-pull`'s body is the only other 9:16 plate wide enough to hold one without narrowing what the writer may write — `structure/end-card` holds 58 characters against closing's 136, so rotating onto it would have shrunk every conclusion in the channel to suit the alternate.

ONE THING AT STATEMENT SIZE. The original close has three lines and a script has one conclusion, so two of them were always empty. The handle moves up to the kicker: this plate's date label sits inside the caption band, where the last spoken words would run over it. Its detail line stays empty — the plate's own caution is not to pad it.
